pairs.evidence: lib/articles/types.ts:689 The trial contract this engine writes posts around decides upheld or challenged only by comparing delta with a declared minimum-effect band, and the per-arm sd and the CI are reported but never decide; nothing checks that the between-arm spread clears the within-arm SD, so with n=3 and a wide sd a band-clearing delta still publishes an order that sits inside the noise (computeVerdict in lib/articles/trial/verdict.ts, in another context, works the same way).

techniques.evidence: lib/articles/types.ts:689 Only the declared band decides (types.ts:624 minEffect). Nothing compares delta with sd before upheld or challenged is emitted, so an order can be published inside the noise.
lib/articles/types.ts:584 Exactly one optimized metric, plus TrialThreshold guards that each arm must clear to win.
lib/articles/types.ts:679 The verdict is code over prereg and results; the model reviewers critique the prose only. engine.ts:18 makes the post check code as well.
lib/articles/types.ts:634 The model-call and wall-time budget is sealed in the prereg, and going over it voids the trial. The dry stand-in (dryAgent.ts) is a mock mode at the job level.
lib/articles/types.ts:566 A two-arm question with a declared vocabulary of winners, including null and void, so a tie or a broken protocol is not reported as a win.

pairs.registryProposal: candidate-write-access covers only the CANDIDATE writing to the instrument. Here an agent with a shell and a declared prior (types.ts:617) writes the harness that measures both arms and the results.json the coded verdict reads, and only the prereg is sealed. The technique could name the experimenter-writes-the-measurement surface: an agent arbitrating between two techniques, rather than being scored itself.
